Communication Standard

UNYRA Institutional Communication Style Guide

This guide defines how UNYRA GROUP LLC should sound when communicating with customers, suppliers, brokers, forwarders, banks, customs-related parties, and other external counterparties.

Guide ControlCurrent Standard

PurposeDefine the institutional tone, request language, deadline discipline, escalation wording, closing style, and containment language used in formal UNYRA counterparty communication.

1. Communication ObjectiveLink

Every important external message should communicate the following objectives.

ObjectiveRequired signal
Institutional controlThe message makes the reference, owner, stage, and next action clear.
Commercial clarityThe recipient understands what is being requested, confirmed, released, rejected, or held.
Executive calmThe tone stays measured even when timing, risk, or counterparty behavior is difficult.
Operational precisionDates, deadlines, references, files, and gates are specific.
Disciplined follow-throughThe message shows who owns the next response and what happens if the response is delayed.

The recipient should feel that UNYRA knows exactly what was sent, why it was sent, what happens next, and who owns the next step.

2. Tone StandardLink

Tone to useTone to avoid
FormalCasual
ConciseOverly friendly
RespectfulApologetic without reason
ExplicitVague
MeasuredChat-like
Internationally credibleEmotionally reactive

3. Sentence StyleLink

PreferAvoid
Short paragraphsLong winding explanations
Direct statementsStacked questions in one paragraph
Clean request languagePassive wording when ownership matters
One clear action per sentence when possibleFiller phrases
Concrete deadlinesOpen-ended timing language

4. Subject Line StandardLink

Subject lines should be structured and scannable.

ElementStandard
Preferred format[UNYRA Ref] Clear institutional subject
Reference qualityUse the communication, matter, or release reference when available.
Subject qualityState the reason for the communication without casual wording.

Subject-line examples are listed below.

Example subject lineUse case
[COMM-2026-041] Formal Offer Packet for Review and ConfirmationFormal commercial release requiring review.
[COMM-2026-044-L1] Final Shipment Alignment Confirmation RequiredTime-sensitive shipment confirmation.
[COMM-2026-052] Document Deficiency Notice and Response DeadlineControlled deficiency notice with a response requirement.

5. Opening StandardLink

Open with the following elements.

Opening elementRequired content
Reason for the messageState why UNYRA is writing.
Linked matterIdentify the deal, shipment, packet, payment, compliance, or control reference when relevant.
Response importanceState the response, confirmation, or action needed.

Use this good opening pattern.

UNYRA is issuing this communication in connection with [matter] to confirm [specific purpose].

6. Action Request StandardLink

When asking for action, use verbs that sound controlled.

Controlled verbAppropriate use
ConfirmReceipt, position, timing, release, or status.
ReviewDocuments, terms, packet contents, or proposed next steps.
ApproveFormal authorization or acceptance.
RejectClear refusal or exception response.
AcknowledgeReceipt or awareness without implying full approval.
ProvideMissing documents, evidence, instructions, or payment proof.
ReturnSigned documents, written responses, or completed forms.
AdviseA controlled response where the counterparty must provide direction.

Do not hide the request in soft language.

Use this preferred request pattern.

Please confirm receipt and return your written response by [date and time].

7. Deadline StandardLink

Deadline fieldRequired use
Exact due dateState the actual calendar date.
TimeInclude the time when timing affects release, payment, shipment, compliance, or escalation posture.
TimezoneInclude the timezone when parties may operate across markets.

Use this preferred deadline pattern.

Please provide your written response by [Month Day, Year], at [time] [timezone].

Avoid vague timing unless the matter is genuinely non-urgent.

AvoidReason
as soon as possibleIt creates urgency without an accountable deadline.
soonIt is not operationally measurable.
when convenientIt weakens response discipline.

8. Escalation StandardLink

When silence or delay has consequences, say so in controlled language.

Escalation elementRequired expression
ConsequenceState what may need to be revalidated, held, escalated, or reapproved.
ToneSound firm and disciplined, not threatening.
ScopeAvoid implying a broader consequence than the live control record supports.

Use this preferred escalation pattern.

If confirmation is delayed beyond the stated deadline, UNYRA may need to revalidate pricing, release timing, or packet status.

9. Closing StandardLink

Close with the following elements.

Closing elementRequired content
Return channelTell the recipient where or how to return the response.
Escalation contactInclude the contact when the matter is urgent or controlled.
Institutional closing lineClose cleanly without casual filler.

Preferred closings are listed below.

Preferred closingUse case
We appreciate your timely attention to this matter.General controlled close.
Please return your response against the communication reference above.Reference-driven close.
Should clarification be required, please contact the UNYRA owner identified in this release.Owner-driven close.

10. Prohibited LanguageLink

Do not use language that sounds informal or weak in formal external releases.

AvoidWhy it weakens the release
just checkingSounds informal and non-controlled.
friendly reminderSoftens a formal response requirement.
hope this helpsReads like casual support language.
let me knowHides the specific requested action.
whenever you canRemoves deadline discipline.
sorry to bother youWeakens authority without cause.
quick questionFrames a controlled matter as casual.

11. Signature RuleLink

Signature contextLanguage requirement
Founder signatureThe body should sound founder-grade, controlled, and institutionally final.
Business-development signatureThe body should still sound controlled, premium, and commercially precise.
Any approved UNYRA signature blockThe wording should match the visual authority of the approved signature composition.

13. Containment and Movement LanguageLink

When a deal, shipment, payment, or release path is under contained-movement control, apply these rules.

Containment language ruleRequired behavior
Current movement onlyDescribe only the movement that is actually current and allowed.
Held or revalidated itemsState what remains under review, on hold, or subject to revalidation.
Linked internal control languageUse the same stop rule and next safe movement carried by the linked internal control records.
No broader release implicationAvoid wording that sounds broader, cleaner, or more final than the live gate actually allows.

Use this preferred containment pattern.

UNYRA is maintaining the matter under controlled review, and the next movement step will be reconfirmed against the current release conditions referenced above.

Avoid when the executable-check board, scenario response review, executive risk register, funding review, or pre-shipment gate still carry a narrower answer:

AvoidWhy it is unsafe
the shipment is fully releasedImplies final shipment clearance.
payment is clear to proceedImplies payment release authority.
everything is approvedImplies broader approval than the live gate may support.
